$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ -7 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-7\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$

Consider the vector $\mathbf{v}$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of a $2 \times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda=2+4\textrm{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PCP^{-1}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2 \times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PCP^{-1},$ where 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14244484/assets/09678574c9eef81d738a84d47848dfdcf33e003616d901436349ae6884d6923a.svg)

and $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda.$

First, notice that 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14244484/assets/e01352e3004dee81c8fd073a1eafae79100501aa252a2a2ef2aa8f0cc86aa803.svg)

while

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14244484/assets/d95fab420931c5eb3330491cf534af3a5176026910ba4772a7a644d36eadbfab.svg)

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overline{\lambda}=2-4\textrm{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda.$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overline{\mathbf{v}},$ the complex conjugate of $\mathbf{v}.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ 7\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
